summary: Iteration-8 smart-keypad summon: all 6 backend scenarios PASS (pytest 16/16 incl. iter7 regression). Frontend mobile UI verified: LIGHT phrase skips keypad and shows room card; leaving a room via back button correctly resets the home tab to the idle state; DEEP phrase correctly shows the PIN keypad. However, one functional bug found: after entering the PIN and tapping 'Summon room', the DEEP room is NOT returned because the frontend passes the GestureResponderEvent as the `skipPin` argument (onPress={summon}), which makes the request body omit the `pin` field. Backend confirmed working via direct curl with the same phrase+pin.

ui_bugs.issue: onPress={summon} passes the press event as the first arg (skipPin), causing the request body to drop the `pin` field. Result: backend returns rooms=[], pin_required=true and the keypad stays. Fix: change to onPress={() => summon()} on line 449.

integration_issues.flow: DEEP room summon (phrase -> keypad -> PIN -> summon)
integration_issues.issue: Backend receives request without `pin` field even though user entered a 4+ digit PIN. Verified via page.expect_response: POST /api/rooms/summon returns {rooms:[], join_candidate:null, pin_required:true} for the user's own Deep room when they should have unlocked it. Direct curl with the same {phrase, pin} returns the room correctly, confirming the bug is purely frontend.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecated package warning in expo logs and console: '[expo-av]: Expo AV has been deprecated and will be removed in SDK 54. Use the `expo-audio` and `expo-video` packages.' Reference: frontend uses expo-av; should migrate to expo-audio / expo-video.
Console warning: 'Image: style.resizeMode is deprecated. Please use props.resizeMode.' Reference: some <Image> usage in frontend (multiple screens emit this on render).
Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents.' Reference: index.tsx or shared component using <View pointerEvents=...>.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx line 449: change `onPress={summon}` to `onPress={() => summon()}` so the press event is not passed as the `skipPin` boolean. This currently breaks every Deep-mode summon.
Audit other `onPress={fnWithDefaults}` patterns in the same file (and codebase) for the same trap. Same concern applies wherever a callback has default arg values (e.g., leaveRoom, summon helpers).
Migrate expo-av to expo-audio / expo-video (expo-av deprecated in SDK 54).
Replace deprecated View pointerEvents prop with style.pointerEvents.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /rooms/summon (lines 718-800): logic is correct and privacy-safe — `pin_required` is only set when the user is a MEMBER of a Deep room with that phrase; non-members get `pin_required=False` for both unmatched and Deep-room-they-don't-know-about phrases. Verified by test_deep_non_member_no_pin_leak.

Frontend `summon` callback design is fragile: it accepts `(skipPin=false, fromPhraseStep=false)` and is used both as a direct handler (which breaks) and as a programmatic call. Recommend either: (a) always wrap in arrow, or (b) split into two named functions `summonWithPin()` and `summonPhraseOnly()`.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx line 449, `onPress={summon}` directly references the function `summon(skipPin=false, fromPhraseStep=false)`. React Native's Pressable/Button invokes onPress with a GestureResponderEvent as the first argument. JavaScript then binds that event object to `skipPin`. Because the event object is truthy, two things go wrong: (1) the validation `if (!skipPin && pin.length < 4)` is bypassed; (2) the ternary `body: skipPin ? { phrase } : { phrase, pin }` evaluates to `{phrase}`, dropping the user's PIN. The backend therefore sees a phrase-only request and correctly answers `{rooms:[], pin_required:true}`. Mitigation: wrap as `onPress={() => summon()}` (or `onPress={() => summon(false)}`). Verified by capturing the POST /api/rooms/summon response via Playwright `page.expect_response`: body was `{rooms:[], join_candidate:null, pin_required:true}` and a direct curl with `{phrase, pin:'4567'}` returned the Deep room — proving backend works and the regression is purely frontend.
